name: SubQuery Settings missing setter authorization
summary: Settings.setContractAddress() and setBatchAddress() lacked owner checks, so five transactions installed attacker-controlled critical-role addresses and used the resulting StateChannel, staking, rewards, token, and booster authority to drain Treasury funds, pooled stake, deployment boosters, and 272 approved wallets.
notes: The Settings proxy's creation transaction emitted its only pre-anchor Upgraded event, selecting implementation 0xf282737992da4217bf5f8b6ae621181e84d7d3b9. Its EIP-1967 slot and the implementation's runtime hash remained unchanged through the pre-anchor block.

Exact stolen SQT is the sum of attacker-controlled recipients' net increases across the five loss receipts: 7,123.035017761666600000; 218,070,478.035174175990999309; 11,819,839.568823074202091517; 22,811,586.289378905375499424; and 129,364,800.151362385762131451 SQT. It excludes 359,614.732487847483438659 SQT of withdrawal fees retained by the protocol Treasury, which explains the difference from SubQuery's rounded 382,433,441 SQT gross-withdrawal figure. The latest CoinGecko observation before the anchor values the stolen amount at $220,502.84.
